title: Validate a binary search tree
summary: In this orchard every tree to the left must be smaller and every tree to the right larger, than every ancestor, not just the parent.
goal: Decide whether the orchard follows the ordering rule everywhere

mapping.formal: An open range (low, high) from its ancestors

examples.label: A child breaks it
examples.explanation: 4 is the right child of 5 but is smaller than 5.

examples.label: An ancestor breaks it
examples.explanation: 3 sits in 5's right subtree, so it must be larger than 5, even though it is fine under 6.

ladder.name: Check every node against its whole subtrees
ladder.idea: For each node, check that everything in its left subtree is smaller and everything in its right subtree is larger.

ladder.name: Read the orchard in order
ladder.idea: Visit left subtree, node, right subtree; a valid search tree produces strictly increasing values.
ladder.insight: A binary search tree read left-node-right is sorted, and checking a list is sorted is one pass.

ladder.name: Carry the allowed range down
ladder.idea: Pass each node the range its value must lie in. Going left lowers the upper limit to the node's value; going right raises the lower limit.
ladder.insight: Each node only needs to know the tightest limits set by its ancestors, two numbers, not the whole subtree. Checking against them catches rules broken by distant ancestors.

transfer.problem: A file system says every folder's files are alphabetically between the folder's neighbours above. Check a nested listing follows that rule.
transfer.explanation: Carry the allowed range down the hierarchy and check each entry against its inherited limits.

selfCheck: Checks every node against limits from all ancestors, not just its parent.
Treats an empty tree as valid.
